problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-4}\,i+t\,j+\sqrt{t-2}\,k.$

feedback.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=⟨3{t}^{3}-1,\,(t+1)^{2},\,\sqrt{t+9}⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $3{t}^{3}-1$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $(t+1)^{2}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\sqrt{t+9}$ is $t\in [-9,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14033854/assets/7c424889be78d14cca345aabd0c1f8289d7bba4c893a17feb6855540cad337fe.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in [-9,\infty ).$
